requirement: Describe a randomized controlled mechanistic study in older adults undergoing total knee arthroplasty, comparing five weeks of quadriceps neuromuscular electrical stimulation with a control receiving standard rehabilitation without a study NMES device.

evidence.text: The aims and methods define the TKA cohort, randomized NMES comparison, duration, and control condition.

requirement: Randomize participants 1:1 to NMES or control using covariate-adaptive allocation incorporating age, BMI, sex, and surgeon.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies 1:1 covariate-adaptive randomization using age, BMI, sex, and surgeon.

requirement: Plan 32 participants per randomized group and state that the 25% overall attrition allowance is intended to yield 24 evaluable participants per group.

evidence.text: The methods specify n=32 per group with 25% attrition to reach n=24 per group.

requirement: For Aim 1, assess pre-surgery to five-week post-TKA changes in muscle fiber size and function, including MHC I and IIA fiber cross-sectional area, tension and velocity, plus intermyofibrillar and subsarcolemmal mitochondrial content.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the mechanistic Aim 1 outcomes and baseline/five-week timing.
The SAP specifies the fiber and mitochondrial primary outcomes.

requirement: For Aim 2, assess the NMES treatment effect on the same muscle structural and functional outcomes as a group-by-time effect from pre-surgery to five weeks after TKA.

evidence.text: The protocol states that Aim 2 tests whether NMES prevents early structural and functional adaptations.
The SAP defines the primary group-by-time analysis.

requirement: Distinguish the primary five-week evaluation from the optional two-week mechanistic assessment and the six-month follow-up of whole-muscle and whole-body function.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies the primary, optional, and longer-term assessment roles.

requirement: For Aim 1, fit a general linear mixed model to control-group pre-surgery and five-week data with a participant random effect for measurements such as multiple fibers nested within participants and allow prespecified person-level covariates at level 2.

evidence.text: The SAP describes a two-level mixed model with within-patient clustering.

requirement: For Aim 2, fit a general linear mixed model with NMES versus control as the between-participant factor, pre-surgery versus five weeks as the within-participant factor, and test the group-by-time interaction.

evidence.text: The SAP defines the Aim 2 mixed model and primary interaction.

requirement: Collapse outcomes having multiple observations per participant to a participant-level mean when an analysis requires one value per participant, while preserving hierarchical modeling where specified.

evidence.text: The SAP says variables with multiple observations per subject will be collapsed to a single mean value.

requirement: Compare dropouts with completers and conduct best- and worst-case response sensitivity analyses for dropout impact, with the exact conservative-response construction fixed before unblinding.

evidence.text: The SAP assumes random dropout but calls for dropout comparison and most/least conservative sensitivity analyses.

requirement: Evaluate sex as an additional effect and use mediation analysis only when an upstream TKA or NMES effect is observed, to assess whether fiber-level changes mediate whole-muscle or whole-body functional changes.

evidence.text: The SAP conditionally specifies sex-effect and mediation analyses.

requirement: Do not interpret the six-month measurements as a second efficacy endpoint for NMES; use them to examine whether early preservation predicts longer-term functional improvement.

evidence.text: The protocol explicitly limits the six-month assessment to prediction rather than long-term treatment efficacy.

requirement: Define randomized, treated, evaluable, biopsy, optional-two-week, and safety analysis populations and bind each outcome and model to one population.

evidence.text: The protocol describes enrollment, intervention, biopsies, and optional testing but not complete analysis-set definitions.

requirement: Specify the primary outcome hierarchy, treatment contrast, null hypotheses, alpha, confidence intervals, covariance structure, degrees-of-freedom method, and study-level success rule before analysis.

evidence.text: The protocol identifies several coequal mechanistic outcomes but does not define an inferential hierarchy or success rule.

requirement: Define multiplicity control across fiber type, structural and functional outcomes, two aims, subgroup effects, and mediation analyses, or label nonprimary analyses exploratory.

evidence.text: Many mechanistic outcomes and analyses are listed without a multiplicity plan.

requirement: Prespecify missing-data and outlier handling, covariate-selection rules, distributional transformations, mediation assumptions, and the numerical best/worst-case dropout values rather than choosing them after seeing data.

evidence.text: The protocol does not provide these operational analysis rules.
The SAP allows covariates and conservative dropout scenarios without fully prespecifying selection or values.
